lines: The landslip's gone? Then the line to Cogsworth runs. Go and tell the tinkerers we're still here.
Clear water! I'd forgotten what the well sounds like.
A man in a good coat came through this morning offering Glint for 'starlight', if we found any. I said we hadn't.
I didn't like his coat.
The col's under shard crows, last I heard. Free them and take the loaf up the Col Path.
The halt's platform first, then the Millrace cutting. The slip's full of boars dug in for the winter.
The well's mark is by the lantern. Rubble mostly, and one very surprised frog.
The hut warden's at the Col hut, up past the col. She likes the crust.
A train to Cogsworth! I'll need to order things. I'd forgotten I could order things.
We held! The whole square held!
Now, the train. Valley Halt's platform is matchwood and the Millrace cutting's under a landslip.
Fix both and Cogsworth's a morning's ride away. They'll have news. Tinkerers always have news.
The warden's fed? Good. Now our well. It's still full of the storm.
Clear it at the mark by the lantern and we'll have water on the square again.
Before the storm the hut warden came down from the Frostline every week for a loaf. She hasn't come since.
Here, take her one. The ridge col's full of shard crows, so go ready.
Here they come, down the halt road. Stand by the lantern with me. We'll see them off together.
Did you hear them? Howling all night, and not one of them reached the lantern. Not one!
Ring when you're ready, not before. The bell tells them we're waiting.
A ring on the green, a stove beside it. The hut warden's idea? I can tell. It's very sensible and very cold.
The bell cupola's mark is on the library. Get it up and we'll hear them coming.
A bell, a ring, a lantern with three lights in it. If my grandmother could see this square.
That lantern's too bright to miss now, and the moor's noticed. The wolves were howling at it last night.
Get the library's bell back up so it can warn us, and we'll meet them on the square.
The jars are back on the shelves, mostly the right way up. Come by before you go out. I'll fill your flasks.
A roof! I can hear the rain on it and none of the rain on me.
I'll brew for the town. But the fever in those creatures comes from the light, and the light is out there.
Take me with you. Somebody has to see what it does up close, and I'd rather it was someone who takes notes.
The mark's on my door. Timber and slates. Then I can brew again.
You're back. Good. My roof is still in the bakery's yard, and my jars are still on the floor.
Help me put it on again and the herbalist's is an apothecary. Tonics for the road.
Three great shards hum together. The light runs down into the well and, faintly, up the stair toward the woods.
The lantern's light has gone up to the circle. It still glows, softer now, like a coal kept for the morning.
You lift the Frostline's shard into a cradle. Frost runs along the iron, then melts.
You lift the moor's shard into a cradle. For a moment the square smells of heather.
Every stone is warm to the touch.
The stones hum. One in the ring is not a stone at all: it is turning its head.
The light comes up the stair behind you and runs into the stones. The ground shakes. Something in the ring wants to see what you're made of.
Old standing stones, moss to the knee. They feel like they're listening.
Fourteen stones. A few are lit. I am counting. Stones are good at waiting.
You stood well. The circle had to know.
I have stood here since before the valley had a name. The light in your lantern is the light we were built to hold.
There is more of it out there. I would like to walk, for once. Slowly, if you don't mind.
The bell hangs quiet, one ear cocked for trouble.
You ring the bell. Across the square shutters close, lamps go out, and Hale picks up her hammer.
The bell hangs in its new frame. Ring it when you're ready.
An empty cupola on the library roof. The bell lies in the street below it.
The light's burning and the boats are coming home. Now, where is the next dark place?
You lit it. I saw it from the quay, turning, the way it should.
I keep that light so boats find their way past what's in the water. There's more in the water now than rocks.
Wherever the rest of those shards fell, someone will need a light. I'd like it to be mine. May I come?
Driftwood's down the harbour road. Mind the quay. Whatever's on it bites.
Velvet. I keep the Driftwood light. Since the storm the quay is overrun and the lamp is out.
There are shards in the bay now, and boats out there with no way home. Help me light it again?
The lamp turns slowly, throwing its beam across the bay.
You trim the wick and light the lamp. The great lens turns, and its beam swings out over the water.
A cold lamp behind a great glass lens.
The apothecary is open.
You pay 40 Glint for timber and slates. By evening the roof is back on and Morel is sweeping up glass.
Half the roof is in the bakery's yard. Putting it back needs 40 Glint of timber and slates.
Clear water, all the way down.
You pay 20 Glint for rope and a hired barrow. The rubble comes out, and one very surprised frog.
The well is choked with rubble. Clearing it needs 20 Glint for rope and a barrow.
The training yard is open, its stove lit.
You pay 40 Glint. New posts, a fresh rope, and a little stone stove on the north side, out of the wind.
The old ring on the green is flattened. Rebuilding it needs 40 Glint.
The bell is back in its cupola.
You pay 50 Glint. Hale and two neighbours haul the bell back up and fix it in a new frame.
The library's bell lies in the street. A new frame and a hoist need 50 Glint.
The platform is whole again.
You pay 60 Glint for sleepers and planks. The platform goes back up, lamp and all.
The platform is matchwood. Rebuilding it needs 60 Glint of sleepers and planks.
